builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: ProQuant: Progressive Quantization-aware Training for Edge MLLMs
summary: ProQuant replaces post-training quantization (and prior QAT) for low-bit multimodal LLMs with a weight-activation QAT pipeline using self-relabeled training data and progressive block activation that prioritizes recovering multimodal understanding layers first. The cost is a full quantization-aware finetuning run with curated, self-relabeled data, which is substantially more compute- and engineering-intensive than PTQ methods such as GPTQ or AWQ and strains a single 24 GB GPU budget for 2B-8B vision-language models. Failure modes include distribution mismatch if the self-relabeling degrades data quality, reliance on the vision-sensitive layer identification generalizing to other architectures, and residual accuracy loss on tasks where the ~1% gap concentrates.
rationale: The accuracy gains at W4A8 are compelling for edge deployment, but the method requires a QAT training pipeline with relabeled data that exceeds the reader's constrained compute, so it is worth tracking rather than adopting until quantized checkpoints or lighter variants appear.
technique: Progressive QAT for low-bit edge MLLMs

The cost is a full quantization-aware finetuning run with curated, self-relabeled data, which is substantially more compute- and engineering-intensive than PTQ methods such as GPTQ or AWQ and strains a single 24 GB GPU budget for 2B-8B vision-language models. Failure modes include distribution mismatch if the self-relabeling degrades data quality, reliance on the vision-sensitive layer identification generalizing to other architectures, and residual accuracy loss on tasks where the ~1% gap concentrates.
W4A8 Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct improves average accuracy by 6.6 points over existing PTQ/QAT baselines and comes within roughly 1% of the full-precision model.
